This is my first review for a game I am about to give.  Please don't flag me as a bot Metacritic because of this.  I played the game on Survivor difficulty and it took me 33 hours 41 minutes to complete. I feel like I have earned the opinion I am about to give.,,Story(Spoilers): I started the game off vaguely hearing of the spoilers, knowing what happens to Joel, but not how it happens.  That was the extend of my previous knowledge.  I noticed friction between Joel and Ellie.  I knew something went down between them where Ellie was not happy and Joel was slightly heart broken.  The acting in this game was very good when you can convey such emotion in your face without needing to say words.  I was broken inside after seeing what happened to Joel.  Every person who saw this had the same heartbroken and shocked reaction that I did.  We all hated Abby at that moment, but I'll get to talking about her later. Ellie and Dina had a sweet relationship in this game.  There were some genuinely nice moments they had together.  I didn't like how in the first 10 minutes of playing the game I was reminded 4 times of Ellie being a lesbian through a bigot and other comments made.  Having genuine sweet moments of people in love holds more weight than making them feel like the world doesn't agree with their choices. Ellie is out for revenge and the story progresses rather well through the days leading up to finding Abby.  I was forced to kill dogs in this game, which I wasn't happy to do, but I do understand in war these things happen.  I love my current dog(Apollo) dearly and understand how it can affect people.  When we finally catch up with Abby she is as evil as ever.  We know why she wants to kill Ellie with all the terrible things Ellie did to Abby's friends.  We just don't care.  Ellie is who we saved from that hospital because of the love Joel had for her.  We understand we doomed the world, but we just don't care.  The best line from Abby's point of view was when we had the flashback to the day of the surgery.  Abby's father is asked if it was his daughter could he do the same thing.  Knowing his daughter would die on the table.  Her father never answered the question directly.  He just danced around it.  When the time came where we had to play as Abby the entire community had the same reaction, disgust.  We don't care who is was leading up to that point.  The only question I had was how she because so ripped though.  To get that built as a guy it takes consuming massive amounts of high protein/low carb foods.  For a woman it is even harder to achieve.  How angry would you be when there are people starving out in the world and some one decides to eat 4 times what others do just to maintain that build? I mean doesn't she have to go on missions?  She would need to reserve possibly 8 hours a day to maintain that.  A perfect example is the end of the game when she losing all that muscle from starvation.  Anyways, at first I thought it might be a mission or two where I would play as Abby, but when I noticed the days progressing the same way as Ellie's story line I was not happy.  I don't care if she throws balls for dogs or befriends some scars.  When Abby's long portion finally ended we finally get a nice part where Ellie is second mother to Dina's baby.  It's nice has Ellie seems happy at first, but than you realize that she suffers from PTSD.  Tommy shows up and gives information on how to find Abby to finish things finally. I can best describe Ellie as a soldier who just never left the war.  She is so damaged inside that she doesn't know how to live in peace.  This happens to people all the time.  Ellie leaves her for one last mission and after finding Abby, rescuing Abby, than forgiving Abby for killing Joel she heads back to an empty house.  No Dina and no baby.  The final scene shows the last conversation Ellie and Joel had before that terrible chain of events happened.,,What started as a review ended up being a therapeutic release of my feeling towards this game.  Does this game deserve a 10/10 by the scared game critics who don't want to lose the influence of Naughty Dog?  No way.  Does it deserve a 0/10? Not that either.  If Abby was turned into a character more similar to Owen than I would have been happy.  She would have seen the flaws in constantly being at war and just got tired of it.  She sides with Ellie in a fight against a new enemy that has Joel die tragically trying to save Abby from this other threat.  I didn't go into the game wanting to hate Abby.   Naughty Dog did it for me and tried so hard to change my mind, but never succeeded.,,The failure was not in the graphics, acting or game play.  It was in the story.  It had potential, but Naughty Dog dropped the ball and it rolled under the fence.  Leaving us all as sad puppies.

But, it will feel not as polished as other more stealth based games.,- AI is ok, but feels very outdated and not any different than any other games.,,Bad aspects:,- Overall story, was a major let down for me. A clichéd dogma seems to have manifested - that if you do not like or appreciate this game's storytelling, you're too ignorant to comprehend its symbolism or complexity. Couple this with the prevalent bigoted comments, there seems to be little focus on rational criticisms aside from a quick acknowledgement that a few exist. Instead, the more exhaustive discussions often seem to digress into this belief that the majority of scrutiny has an ulterior, alt-right motive (beknownst to the reviewer or not). While it is important to talk about considering it could very well be true, the toxic and polarizing result leaves little room left for those valid critiques.,,And I (among several others I've spotted) thought there were huge problems with the game that aren't nested in anti-progressive attitudes...,,On the vaccine - my interpretation (and it could be wrong) of the first game was that this was nothing more than fleeting hope amongst an incredibly desperate rag-tag group of abused and abusive individuals. There was little, if any, inductive evidence provided to suggest that one could actually be derived from Ellie, aside from minor lip-service. There was no invitro-testing, data analysis, or even procurement of proper scientific equipment to produce one, presented/mentioned in the storyline. Then there's the manufacturing, development, adverse-event monitoring, and proper coordination of conveying this information to other researchers/physicians (and how many of those are left?) across the continent in order to vaccinate everyone, assuming there would be no other unforeseen phenomenon, catastrophes, wars over the drug, etc… All in all, the science was left to your imagination, which is fine, but my imagination never really lead me to believe that, in this universe as presented, it was viable. So I understood (though didn't necessarily agree) with Joel's motivations in the first game, and why I felt that his lie to Ellie was so moving at the end.,,I'm unsure if the story of LOUII was already planned during the development of the first. If so, I think the first one should've been handled differently. If not, then I'm not clear as to why so much weight was given to the effectiveness of the vaccine, as it was never construed to be. This trivializes the ethical justification for Abby - as I do not truly believe she was utilitarian, nor her father. Thus, it's hard to agree an "eye for an eye" was ever properly indicated, which I think was the intent of this revenge plot.,,So I didn't really like the story for that main reason. The gameplay was also a bit boring -- it just felt dated, and perhaps there were just too many interactive cinematic parts. I strongly disliked the soundtrack... I didn't find any of the (very few) tracks moving, aside from a few pieces, and most of the game you trudge through silence. Though the actual sound effects were solid, as was the voice acting.,,Graphics, on the other hand, were brilliant. It's a shame I can't get as much FPS as I'd like from a PS4, but nonetheless, they were absolutely phenomenal!,,Overall - I'd give this game a 3/10. The main value resulting from the artistic portrayal of the environments. It wasn't really fun to play, the story was a bit too long, and the motif of revenge has been done better before. At $60... that's asking too much for the quality that it is...

As someone who absolutely adored the first game, I genuinely want to throw up from how disappointing part 2 is. I waited for this sequel for 4 years (some people have waited longer), and I talked it up so much, it pains me deeply to write this review. A 4 is probably the most accurate rating this game deserves. The good parts:,-The music is incredible. Their music composer, Gustavo Santaolalla, the same person that made the first game’s music, is a genius. The music is very emotional and aids what’s happening on the screen perfectly. -The sound design is definitely pleasing and not unrealistic in the slightest. Everything, even things you wouldn’t expect to have a sound have one. They’re very crisp and make the game that more enjoyable. Sound is a huge factor in a game, and in this one it’s fantastic.,-The graphics are nothing short of beautiful. The textures are realistic and very lovely to look at. The look of the characters are the most believable I’ve ever seen. Definitely some of the best, if not THE best graphics right now. -The atmosphere is outstandingly well made. Being in a city, traveling through a forest, being underground, and traversing through abandoned buildings are just a few examples that are authentic to real life. Nothing is worse than not being immersed in a game. This one does it perfectly. -The animations are the best you can find at the moment. It’s incredible how much work was put into perfecting the animations. There can be so many different animations for one action, it feels so nice to play. The way the characters move and overall feel is extremely realistic, I never once doubted it.,-The level design is easily the best on the market. Every single scene is different. The insides of buildings to the forests are so well detailed, you can tell how much heart and soul they put into it. The variety of structures and areas to explore is outstandingly well crafted. It’s a huge breathe of fresh air and very fun to explore. -The acting is better than most movies. I said it. The actors Naughty Dog hired are extremely talented. Mainly Ashley Johnson, aka Ellie. She needs to be a main character in a movie, c’mon! The game’s cutscenes are honestly like watching a movie too. Their screams, cries, and overall tone of speaking is perfect for what’s happening on the screen. Easily the best acting in a video game to date. -The versatility in the gameplay is fantastic. You can use so many different items at your disposal to utterly destroy your enemies, or sneak right past them as if you were never there. The choice is up to you. You can go prone, cut through tiny sections in the walls, and jump across platforms. It feels very smooth and grounded, and there never once is a dull moment in the middle of battle.,-The enemies are so well programmed, they feel real. The things they say and how they approach to killing you is great, and very stressful at times! This includes the infected enemies, not just the human ones. -I didn’t encounter one single bug throughout the entirety of the game. Bugs and glitches can really break the immersion in a video game, believe me. Thankfully the testers knew what they were doing and made sure the player never encounters them. Can’t say the same for a lot of other games.,-This game is 30 hours long. That’s very good for a story driven game.,Now, with all these pros, how could this game possibly be a 4? Here’s how:,-The story -The characters and the development of them. How could such a minimal amount of things possibly make this game THAT bad? I ask myself the same thing. How, after all those pros, Naughty Dog managed to mess up the most preordered Ps4 game of all time? It’s simple. A bad story can break a game. A good story can make a game. Unfortunately, this game has a bad story. The entirety of the first game, we’re spent bonding with Joel and Ellie. They are what MADE the first game. The story in the first game is arguably one of the best ever made. In this sequel, their relationship is practically thrown away. The potential this sequel had with such legendary characters like Joel and Ellie could’ve made this game go down in history like the first one, too bad their relationship is not even utilized. Joel is basically a side character in this game. The execution of some scenes were very, very poor and simply mediocre at best. It’s hard to describe the bad parts of this game without spoiling anything, but I’m trying my best. How some characters act is completely and utterly unrealistic to this world and to them, which totally breaks the immersion and your heart at the same time. 40% of 30 hours is the amount of time you’re spent playing someone you absolutely hate. Let’s not forget the ending. The ending is easily the biggest part of a game. If you screw it up, you screw the whole thing up. That’s what they did. It’s so unsatisfying and disappointing, I cried from how much I disliked it. My heart is aching.

The Last of Us Part II,,I've spent a lot of time contemplating a review of this particular game.  I don't usually review games in general on any forum - thus this being my first Metacritic review - some will claim "review bomb" but this is not the case, please hear me out.,,The first installment of this game was a masterpiece, it featured lovable characters that many people (including myself) became attached to, just as in other games like Tomb Raider, but with the added emotional character attachment that oft doesn't develop, or at least not on such a deep level in video games.  Along with the great narrative and exciting adventure that made TLoU so great.,,When I heard ND was making a TLoU2 I was excited to continue this adventure with the beloved characters I had become emotionally attached to, however this game took a turn for the worse early in my playthrough as the series' main protagonist fate was revealed.,,I wasn't a fan of the new characters, and it certainly wasn't what I thought I would be playing when I pre-ordered The Last of Us 2.  As I was playing through I often thought to myself that this should have been a new IP, maybe named "Vengeance" or something rather than marketing it as TLoU2, it seems kind of like a bait and switch to me.  In addition the gratuitous violence was on a new level, I'm sure this was what ND was going for but I wasn't a fan of it.,,The game play was somewhat improved over the original while not being top notch, I was not unhappy with that aspect nor was I unhappy with the visuals or the environments as I prefer more linear games.  The animations were top notch, however I did feel the game was too long, it could have been half the play-time and achieved the same end result. About half way through I was ready for the credits to roll.,,I can't help but feel as I stated before that this should have been a new IP, which I think would have had more positive reviews, but a TLoU game this is not thus the low review score.,,Here's my take:,,Graphics: 9/10 - very good,Environment: 7/10 - very good,Animations: 9/10 - top notch,Mechanics: 5/10 - good enough for the type of game it is,Narrative: 0/10 - not good, not TLoU,Characters: 1/10 - I barely remember their names let alone like them, other than Ellie,Play-time: 3/10 - too long,Gore: 0/10 - excessive and unnecessary,Marketing: 0/10 - misleading,,In conclusion I will just say this, I'm disappointed with the game and ND, you're better than this!  And I look forward to more masterpieces like Uncharted, but I'll probably not be buying any more TLoU games in the future.

The game's story is really about the endless circle of violence due to a ''revenge vendetta''. I believe the aim is to show the destructiveness and truly ugly nature when one goes down such a path.,Sadly, the game actually fails to deliver that goal in a meaningful way and I'll explain why.,,At the start, it tries to anger the player by using a beloved character like Joel as the catalyst that should anger you enough and put you in the mindset of seeking revenge. It's the reason his death is so demeaning and horrible, otherwise if he had a heroic end you'd feel sad but not really pissed off and I get that. The real problem is what comes after and how it's handled. Instead of the game taking you through a trip of violence and allow you to make hard choices at the end of grizzly violent encounters that has a chance to shift your ''revenge at all costs mindset'', it takes a rigid linear approach. It doesn't provide opportunities to the player to test and see if your mindset shifts. For example this is something the Witcher 3 did so excellently where despite what you thought was the right course and good intention, you ended up with a less clear cut result making you question your choices. Instead of short, violent and shocking encounters that have deep impact (because the game is so over-bloated), that violence loses it's shock value and becomes casual which works against what they're trying to achieve. Even when they're trying to 'humanise' Ellie's adversaries, it's done in a wrong way that feels contrived rather than letting you experience it whilst playing as Ellie. Instead they put you right in the boots of her adversary which doesn't work well.,,In the end, instead of building an experience that let's you question this cycle of violence and built up a culminating moment where you get to choose whether you end it by letting the ' main adversary' live or complete your revenge by killing her and continuing that circle...it chooses for you. This is the ultimate failure where turning the game into a preaching session instead of a lesson at the end of which you decide what to take away from it. This falls short of the excellent ending of the first game which allowed the player to walk away with their own interpretation of weather Joel was right or wrong.,,Sure, the graphics are very good and the animations amazing, but the core mechanics and gameplay are not certainly not engaging enough  for the length of time you're required to use them to finish the story. The game is of course technically accomplished and very polished which is not something we're used to as much these days.,,Ultimately, it's not really the type of story that they chose to tell, nor the killing of one of the most beloved characters in gaming (very much inspired by Glen's end in The walking dead), but rather their failure to provide a similarly meaningful payoff and satisfaction for the audience after such a shock move. In the end it feels like a very shallow, uninspiring revenge story.
